title: Clinical Practice Lead
description:
Mission

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear.

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose

The Practice Manager owns practice management for Neko Health's United States professional corporation. The role covers four areas: provider credentialing, SOP organization and maintenance, onboarding operationalization, and compliance assurance. Neko runs a tech-enabled clinical model, and this role is expected to run all four through systems and automation rather than manual tracking.

Credentialing: the role holds the credential file for every provider practicing under the PC: license, certification, permitted scope by state, malpractice coverage details and every other expirable, verified at source and kept current so that no provider ever sees a member on a lapsed credential. While Neko does not credential with payers today - this role runs the credentialing gate that clears a provider to practice and removes that clearance when a credential lapses. It supplies provider credentialing data into the clinic compliance systems and works to the credentialing standard and clear-to-practice definition set by the Head of Compliance.

SOPs: the role owns the SOP library for US practice operations. The role keeps every SOP current, versioned, and easy to find, and retires SOPs that no longer apply.

Onboarding: the role turns each new provider's onboarding plan into a working, tracked sequence: credentialing, system access, training, and clearance to start, in the right order and against a clear timeline.

Compliance: the role checks that US practice operations meet the standards set by the Head of Compliance, and reports gaps as they surface.

Systems and automation: the role chooses, configures and owns the tooling that carries all of the above — one source of truth for provider data, automated expiry alerts, and workflows that hand off cleanly between Talent Acquisition, the People Team, IT and clinical operations. Status should be visible from the system rather than assembled by hand.

As Neko opens further states, credentialing volume and complexity grow faster than headcount, and practice operations grow with them. This role exists to make provider readiness, SOP currency, onboarding execution, and compliance standing a managed process with evidence behind it, built on tooling that scales faster than headcount, rather than a scramble before each launch.

What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

  • A current, auditable register of every clinician's license, credential, and permitted scope by state, held in a single system of record with automated expiry tracking and a named process for renewal before lapse.

  • A complete credential file per provider practicing under the PC, with primary source verification evidence attached and dated.

  • A written credentialing procedure covering intake, verification, the clear-to-practice decision, re-verification cycle, and removal of clearance.

  • The credentialing gate built into the clinician onboarding sequence, so a start date cannot be confirmed without verified credentials.

  • A current SOP library for US practice operations: indexed, version-controlled, and reviewed on a set cycle.

  • An onboarding operations sequence that turns each new provider's plan into a tracked timeline from offer to start, with the credentialing gate built in.

  • Practice operations running in-system rather than on spreadsheets: onboarding, SOP review cycles and compliance checks tracked in Neko's tooling, with the remaining manual steps documented and a plan to remove them.

  • A compliance status report showing where US practice operations meet the Head of Compliance's standards, and where they do not, generated from the system rather than compiled by hand.

Key Responsibilities

Provider credentialing and primary source verification

  • Run credentialing intake for every new provider joining the PC: application, document collection, and verification at source rather than from candidate-supplied copies.

  • Verify state medical/nursing licenses, board certification, education and training, work history, and DEA registration where the provider's scope requires it.

  • Operate the clear-to-practice gate: no provider is released to see members until the credential file is complete and verified.

  • Maintain the permitted scope by state for each provider and flag to the Head of Compliance any request to practice outside it.

Expirables, re-verification and removal

  • Own the expirables calendar for licenses, certifications, DEA registrations, malpractice coverage and any other time-limited credential, driven by automated alerts rather than manual review.

  • Chase renewals ahead of expiry against defined lead times and escalate when a renewal is at risk.

  • Remove clearance to practice immediately when a credential lapses and notify the clinical rota owner and the Head of Compliance the same day.

  • Run the re-verification cycle so credential files do not silently age.

Systems, tooling and automation

  • Select, implement and administer the tooling that runs practice operations: credentialing records, expiry tracking, onboarding workflow and SOP version control.

  • Replace manual tracking with automated alerts, scheduled reporting and system-driven handoffs, and keep a running list of the steps still done by hand.

  • Define the data structure behind credentialing and onboarding so status can be reported out of the system rather than reconstructed.

  • Work with IT and, where relevant, product and engineering to integrate practice operations data with adjacent systems instead of maintaining parallel spreadsheets.

SOP organization and maintenance

  • Own the SOP library for US practice operations: create, index, and version every procedure.

  • Review each SOP on a set cycle and update it when a process changes.

  • Retire SOPs that no longer apply, and flag processes that run without one.

  • Keep SOPs easy to find and use for the staff who rely on them day to day.

Onboarding operationalization

  • Turn each new provider's onboarding plan into a tracked sequence: credentialing, system access, training, and clearance to start.

  • Own the onboarding timeline from offer to start date, and flag delays before they hit the start date.

  • Coordinate with Talent Acquisition, the People Team, and clinical operations to keep the sequence moving.

  • Improve the onboarding sequence as volume grows, including automation of tracking and reminders.

Compliance assurance

  • Confirm that US practice operations meet the standards set by the Head of Compliance.

  • Run periodic checks against those standards, and report gaps as they surface.

  • Support audits of practice operations with evidence drawn from SOPs, onboarding records, and the credentialing file.

  • Escalate compliance gaps that need action beyond this role.

Credentialing process, data and reporting

  • Keep the credentialing record system accurate and audit-ready, so a credential file can be produced on request without reconstruction.

  • Report credentialing status, upcoming expiries and blocked providers into the Medical Quality reporting cycle, on a set cadence and drawn from the system of record.

  • Improve the credentialing process as volume grows, including automation of tracking and reminders.

  • Prepare the function for payer credentialing and provider enrollment should Neko US move to billing insurance.

About you

Minimum Requirements

  • Experience streamlining clinical or healthcare operations in a tech-enabled environment: you have taken a manual, spreadsheet-run process and rebuilt it as a system-driven workflow, and you can describe what you removed and what changed as a result.

  • Experience working in a clinical operations capacity – where you were responsible for not just executing but building the systems to ensure credentialing, compliance and other clinical operations processes are handled excellently.

  • Confident with operational tooling: you configure and administer the systems you depend on rather than raising a ticket for every change, and you are comfortable working with data, reporting and everyday automation.

  • Direct, hands-on experience of state medical board licensure and clinician credentialing processes, including primary source verification.

  • Experience maintaining a credentialing database or record system to an audit-ready standard.

  • Experience developing, organizing, and maintaining SOPs in a clinical or regulated operations setting.

  • Working knowledge of compliance standards in a healthcare or clinical operations setting, with experience checking operations against them.

  • Precise and persistent administratively

Preferred

  • Experience in a digital health, telehealth or otherwise tech-enabled care setting, where clinical operations run on product and tooling rather than paper.

  • Hands-on experience with credentialing or provider data platforms, and with the workflow and tracking tools used to run operations day to day.

  • Experience working alongside product or engineering teams to specify what operational tooling needs to do.

  • Direct experience provider credentialing in a United States clinical setting, including multi-state credentialing.

  • Experience of credentialing in a newly opened market or a start-up clinical service where the process did not yet exist.

  • Experience building an SOP program from scratch in a growing or newly opened operation.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance

  • 401(k) Retirement Plan

  • Commuter Benefits

  • Wellness Rewards Program

  • Complimentary full Neko scan for you and eligible family members

title: Product Designer (m/f/x)
description:
UP42 was founded in 2019 with a clear purpose: to transform how organizations order, access, and analyze Earth observation data. Our platform brings together the world’s leading geospatial providers, and offers a single touchpoint to access, manage, and process data at scale. From vegetation management and infrastructure monitoring to disaster response, UP42 helps organizations across industries find solutions to complex problems through Earth observation. Our expert support team and detailed documentation guide our users through every step. Since July 2025, UP42 has been a part of Neo Space Group.

We are looking for a Product Designer (m/f/x) to join our Design Team in Berlin. You will be the design partner for one of our product teams, working alongside a Product Manager and engineers to take work from an early idea through to something people use. You will own your projects, hold a high quality bar on complex, data-rich interfaces, and work inside a design system you help keep healthy.
You will enjoy this role if you want real ownership of a product area without carrying a whole platform, and if you like going deep into a genuinely complex domain. Our team is complementary, so your work is visible and the feedback loop is short.

What you will do:

  • Take design work from an early idea through to delivery, proposing solutions to blockers rather than only reporting them.

  • Be the reliable design partner for your product team: the person your PM and engineers come to first.

  • Design for complexity: dense data tables, long-running processes, and workflows where the edge cases matter as much as the main path.

  • Look for evidence before you design: talk to users, read what support and sales already know, look at how the product is actually used, and run tests on your own work.

  • Push to understand the problem before designing a solution, and say so when a brief arrives already shaped as one.

  • Scope your own features, break them into pieces, be roughly right about how long they will take, and flag delays early with a plan B rather than a warning.

  • Contribute to our design system, as everyone on our team does: propose and build components, not only use them.

  • Share your work cross-functionally, take feedback, and iterate; notice improvements inside your area and act on them, instead of waiting to be asked.


Here is a good summary of what we are looking for:

  • Experience delivering product design work end-to-end inside a cross-functional team.

  • Solid interaction (IxD) and visual/UI design skills, with the ability to make complex data and workflows understandable.

  • Strong Figma skills, and a working understanding of how a design system is actually built: how a component is structured, how it behaves, and the rules it has to respect. You will be a contributor to ours, not only a user of it.

  • Experience using research and product evidence to make design decisions: usability tests, customer conversations, support tickets, product data. We are not looking for one particular method.

  • Comfortable telling the difference between what we know and what we are assuming, and willing to say which is which.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity: able to make progress when the picture is still incomplete, and to adjust when what you learn changes the direction.

  • Able to scope your own work and communicate honestly about time, collaborative, feedback-driven, and proactive about the problems you can see.

  • Fluent in English and based in Berlin with hybrid work capability.

Bonus points if you bring:

  • Experience designing geospatial, enterprise, or data-heavy B2B products.

  • Background in UX research, data visualization, or complex workflow design.

  • Knowledge of accessibility and inclusive design.

  • Experience with interactive prototyping.

  • Awareness of current AI tools and emerging opportunities in UX processes, with an understanding of how AI can enhance user outcomes without adding unnecessary complexity.

Let us tell you why UP42 is a good choice:

  • Let’s disrupt the industry: You get the chance to shape the state-of-the-art geospatial processing platform and create a completely new planetary perspective

  • Let’s stay flexible: We practice a hybrid working model - you can choose when to work from the comfort of your home or join your colleagues in our modern office in the heart of Kreuzberg, or even from a global place of your choice up to 90 days per year

  • Let’s win as a team: We’re an inspiring international team working in a fun and productive environment

title: Project Associate - Climate Analytics (PSA-3)
description:
United Nations University (UNU)

The United Nations University (UNU) is a global think tank and postgraduate teaching organization within the United Nations System. UNU engages in policy-relevant research, capacity development, and knowledge dissemination in furtherance of the purposes and principles of the United Nations. The work of UNU contributes to solving pressing global problems that are the concern of the United Nations and its Member States.

 

For the past five decades, UNU has been a source of impartial research on sustainability, human security, and economic development. With hundreds of researchers working at institutes in 12 countries, UNU's expertise spans the full breadth of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals, generating policy-relevant knowledge to effect positive global change. UNU collaborates closely with other UN entities and leading research institutions across the globe. For more information, please visit http://unu.edu

 

The United Nations University’s Institute for Environment and Human Security (UNU-EHS) was established in 2003 in Bonn, Germany. The institute conducts research work focusing on advancing human security and well-being by addressing present and future risks arising from environmental hazards and climate change. Its main areas of work are risk & adaptation and transformation. In addition to its research work, UNU-EH offers education opportunities at the master’s level and hosts a number of international PhD projects and capacity-development courses on global issues of environmental risks and sustainable development. More information about UNU-EHS can be found here: https://unu.edu/ehs.

 

The Munich Climate Insurance Initiative (MCII) is hosted at UNU-EHS and is a research-to-policy and practice innovation lab. MCII aims to support and ultimately influence policy making processes that enhance resilience and protect livelihoods of vulnerable communities, through pioneering risk management and risk transfer solutions (e.g. insurance mechanisms) in combination with other approaches to manage climate related risks. For detailed information, please visit: https://ehs.unu.edu/about/departments/the-munich-climate-insurance-initiative-mcii#overview.

Climate Risk Analytics: The Climate Risk Analytics team manages a portfolio of MCII projects that use quantitative methods to improve understanding of climate risk and inform decision making. The main goals for strategic impact are i) to establish analytics to support decisions in adaptation and risk management, ii) to define the “smart mix” of climate response options, including climate risk insurance and to iii) further operational concepts of improved climate risk management also through academic collaborations.

Responsibilities

Under the authority of the Director of UNU-EHS, the guidance of the Chief Climate Risk Strategist and Head of the MCII Division, the successful candidate will be entrusted with the following tasks:

1.     Research, Analysis and Biofincas Project Deliverables

  • Conduct desk research, literature reviews, mapping exercises and data collection on topics relevant to Biofincas project activities and outputs;

  • Prepare graphics, maps, and other visual materials;

  • Support the adaptation of serious games for capacity-building activities.

 

2.     Project Implementation, Coordination and Progress Tracking

  • Support the tracking and follow-up of assigned Biofincas activities under project components, consortium platforms and in line with agreed workplans, timelines and project requirements;

  • Participate in meetings with project partners and consortium members and document outstanding actions, key decisions and follow-up requirements;

 

3.     Workshops, Capacity Building and Stakeholder Engagement activities for Biofincas

  • Support the administrative and logistical preparation and coordination of workshops, meetings, capacity-building activities and stakeholder events;

  • Support the preparation of background materials, agendas, presentations, summaries for stakeholder engagement activities and any other materials required for meetings and events;

  • Maintain stakeholder contact lists, meeting records, and related project documentation;

  • Support routine communication with project partners, technical experts, government counterparts, research institutions and other stakeholders.

 

4.     Project acquisition and Proposal Development Activities

  • Identify and screen relevant funding opportunities and call for proposals aligned with the established areas of work;

  • Assist in the preparation and drafting of selected sections of project proposals and other funding-related materials;

  • Support communication and follow-up with donors and relevant counterparts regarding requirements, processes and application procedures.

 

5.     Cross-cutting Thematic Support

  • Contribute to activities related to cross-cutting themes including gender, agriculture, and climate across Biofincas project components;

  • Support the integration of relevant themes into research outputs, analysis, and project activities and deliverables;

  • Contribute to activities aligned with the gender strategy of the section and the institute.

 

6. Perform other duties as assigned by supervisor(s)

Key Performance Indicators

  • Timely and high-quality development of inputs related to the climate analytics team effort.

  • High quality and level of engagement with project implementation partners.

  • Effective tracking and follow-up of projects activities, decisions and agreed action points.

  • Quality and relevance of contributions of inputs from project partners and other stakeholder.

  • Maintain strong stakeholder relationships and a high level of trust in UNU-EHS/MCII among research partners, governments, donors, and civil society.

Competencies

Values:

  • Inclusion - Take action to create an environment of dignity and respect for all, regardless of age, culture, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, gender expression, geography, grade, language, nationality, racial identity, religion, sex, sex characteristics, sexual orientation, social origin or any other aspect of identity;

  • Humility - Demonstrate self-awareness and willingness to learn from others;

  • Humanity - Act according to the purposes of the United Nations: peace, dignity and equality on a healthy planet.

Behaviours:

  • Connect and Collaborate - Build positive relationships with others to advance the work of the United Nations and work coherently as One UN;

  • Analyse and Plan - Seek out and use data from a wide range of sources to understand problems, inform decision-making, propose evidence-based solutions and plan action;

  • Deliver Results with Positive Impact - Hold oneself and others accountable for delivering results and making a positive difference to the people and causes that the United Nations serves;

  • Learn and Develop - Pursue own learning and development and contribute to the learning and development of others;

  • Adapt and Innovate - Demonstrate flexibility, agility and the ability to think and act in novel ways.



1) Education and certification

MSc degree or equivalent in environmental sciences, natural resource management, environmental engineering, geography, ecology, or a related field.

2) Required qualifications and experience      

  • Solid understanding of disaster risk reduction and management, and climate change adaptation, and related issues

  • Strong ability to conduct desk research, literature reviews, data collection and qualitative and quantitative analysis and to synthesize information technical reports and project deliverables.

  • Proven experience supporting workshops, meetings, capacity-building activities and stakeholder engagement, including logistical and administrative tasks.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, presentation, organizational and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams and external partners.

3) Desired qualifications and experience

  • At least one (1) year of progressively responsible experience in supporting project coordination, preferably in an international setting.

  • Experience with programming, GIS tools for spatial analysis, data visualization and CLIMADA/ECA is an asset.

  • Experience contributing to technical reports, research outputs, project proposals, or donor reporting is an asset.

  • Work experience in developing countries is an asset.

4) Language Requirements:

  • Fluency in English and Spanish is required.

description:
Über uns

Wie bleibt ein RAG-System präzise, wenn aus tausend Dokumenten hunderttausend werden? Wie orchestriert man mehrere Modellanbieter sauber hinter einer Oberfläche? Während anderswo noch Prototypen gezeigt werden, arbeiten unsere Kunden längst damit - mit ihren Daten, ihren Regeln, gehostet in Deutschland. Als Senior Engineer verantwortest du Kernfunktionen und Architektur unserer Plattform, vom Retrieval bis ins Frontend - und du entwickelst sie so, wie wir arbeiten: AI-gestützt, mit Coding-Agents als Teil des Werkzeugkastens und mit echtem Gestaltungsspielraum für deine Ideen. Du suchst eine Rolle, in der technische Tiefe und Produktverantwortung zusammenkommen? Dann sollten wir uns kennenlernen!


Das gibt es zu tun

  • Architektur & Umsetzung Du entwirfst und skalierst verteilte Systeme und Microservices - immer mit Blick auf Wartbarkeit, Stabilität und die Frage, was in zwei Jahren noch trägt. 
  • KI-Features bauen, die im Alltag halten Du entwickelst die Kernfunktionen unserer Plattform - von RAG-basierten Wissensdatenbanken über KI-Apps für einzelne Fachbereiche bis zu Voice-, Übersetzungs- und Analytics-Funktionen. 
  • Full-Stack liefern Du entwickelst performante APIs, modellierst Daten und Datenbanken und setzt moderne Oberflächen im Frontend um - vom Retrieval bis zur Benutzeroberfläche.
  • Daten, Sicherheit & Mandantenfähigkeit Du modellierst Daten für Multi-Tenancy und rollenbasierte Berechtigungen - so, dass niemand über die KI Zugriff auf etwas bekommt, das er nicht sehen darf. Verschlüsselung, Datenminimierung und Auditierbarkeit denkst du von Anfang an mit. 
  • Betrieb & Observability mitdenken Du sorgst dafür, dass Qualität, Kosten und Verhalten der KI-Features im Betrieb sichtbar bleiben - mit Evaluations, Monitoring und klaren Guardrails, damit die Plattform auch bei wachsender Nutzung stabil und effizient läuft.
  • Komplexität beherrschen Du entwickelst bestehende Systeme weiter, schaffst klare Strukturen und reduzierst technische Schulden dort, wo sie langfristig teuer werden und lässt sie stehen, wo sie es nicht sind. 
  • AI-gestützt entwickeln – und den Standard dafür setzen Du arbeitest selbstverständlich mit Coding-Assistenten und Agenten, holst mehr aus ihnen heraus als Autocomplete und weißt genau, wo ihre Grenzen liegen. Neue Tools und Workflows testest du früh, bewertest sie ehrlich und etablierst im Team, wie wir sie sinnvoll einsetzen.
  • Team & Produkt weiterbringen Du arbeitest eng mit Product Owner, UX und unseren Consultants zusammen, übersetzt echte Kunden-Use-Cases in Technik, machst technische Entscheidungen transparent und bringst unsere Junior Developer durch Code Reviews und Mentoring fachlich weiter. 


Das bringst Du mit

  • Mindestens 5 Jahre Erfahrung in der Entwicklung komplexer Softwaresysteme, idealerweise im KI- bzw. SaaS/Cloud-Umfeld
  • Sehr gute TypeScript-Kenntnisse, Erfahrung mit Node.js und idealerweise Frameworks wie NestJS 
  • Sehr gute Kenntnisse in Softwarearchitektur für verteilte Systeme - Microservices, API-Design, Skalierung 
  • Erfahrung im Frontend, z. B. mit Vue.js, sowie ein gutes Verständnis für Full-Stack-Zusammenhänge 
  • Fundierte Kenntnisse im Umgang mit Datenbanken (z. B. PostgreSQL), Datenmodellierung und Performance-Optimierung 
  • Erfahrung mit Cloud-Plattformen (z. B. AWS), Docker und dem Betrieb von SaaS-Anwendungen 
  • AI-gestütztes Entwickeln ist für dich Alltag: Du arbeitest routiniert mit Coding-Assistenten und -Agenten (z. B. Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot), kennst ihre Grenzen und prüfst generierten Code kritisch, statt ihm zu vertrauen 
  • Du bist nah am Puls der Entwicklung: Du probierst neue Tools, Modelle und Workflows aktiv aus und bringst die guten ins Team - Erfahrung mit agentischen Setups (z. B. Coding-Agents in der Cloud, MCP-Integrationen, automatisierte Reviews) ist ein starkes Plus 
  • Tieferes Verständnis moderner AI-/LLM-Konzepte wie RAG, Function Calling, Embeddings oder Agenten
  • Clean Code, Testing und Code Reviews sind für dich selbstverständlich und du bringst Junior Developers durch Reviews und Mentoring gern fachlich weiter 
  • Du triffst technische Entscheidungen und kannst sie nachvollziehbar vertreten - auf Deutsch und auf Englisch 
  • Erfahrung mit DSGVO, ISO 27001 oder dem EU AI Act sind ein Plus 

Was uns wichtig ist 
Frameworks kann man lernen. Was uns viel wichtiger ist: Verantwortung übernehmen, das Produkt mitdenken, Anforderungen konstruktiv hinterfragen und technische Entscheidungen treffen, die man auch in zwei Jahren noch begründen kann - pragmatisch abgewogen zwischen Perfektion und Geschwindigkeit. Konkret heißt das: Du entwirfst morgens die Architektur für ein neues Feature, reviewst mittags Pull Requests, entwickelst nachmittags selbst und bringst dabei unser Team fachlich weiter. title: Data Engineer / Scientist – Multimodal Clinical Data Integration & AI (m/f/d)
description:
About aiPTO

aiPTO is a TechBio startup spun off from the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), taking on one of medicine's hardest problems: brain cancer. We are building a disruptive approach — pairing next-generation patient-derived living tumor with fit-for-purpose virtual-tumor AI models. By recreating a patient's tumor biology in vitro and decoding it in silico, we aim to revolutionize brain cancer drug discovery and precision medicine. More details can be found on our publications (Individualized patient tumor organoids faithfully preserve human brain tumor ecosystems and predict patient response to therapy, DELPHAI predicts heterogeneous perturbation responses with learned single-cell fitness) and LinkedIn (https://www.linkedin.com/company/aipto/).

The project

aiPTO has been selected as the data and AI partner of a newly funded Horizon Europe consortium that unites world-class neuro-oncologists, pathologists and drug-discovery pioneers across Europe. Together we are generating patient profiles of unprecedented depth: multi-omics, high-resolution digital pathology, 3D imaging and longitudinal clinical records, alongside single-cell drug-perturbation data from patient-derived organoids.

As the first member of our Heidelberg hub, you will build the data engine that turns these massive, disparate streams into AI-ready data atlas — the foundation for virtual tumor models and agentic systems designed to predict patient-specific drug response, decode resistance and reveal drug mechanisms.

What you will do

  • Architect the scientific data engine: design, build and scale the infrastructure that unifies multi-omics, spatial transcriptomics, digital pathology, radiological imaging and clinical data

  • Make data AI-ready: harmonise and standardise multimodal datasets for deep-learning models and agentic workflows, working hand-in-hand with our machine-learning and computer-vision scientists

  • Bridge the disciplines: be the link between wet-lab researchers, clinical oncologists and IT scientists, translating biological questions into data schemas

  • Own rigour and compliance: implement biomedical metadata standards and GDPR-grade governance for sensitive patient data

What you bring

  • PhD, or MSc with 2+ years of experience, in bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science, biomedical engineering or a related quantitative field

  • Demonstrated mastery in structuring and integrating complex biological or clinical datasets; hands-on experience with real-world patient data is a strong plus

  • Depth in at least one modality — multi-omics, spatial biology, digital pathology or medical imaging — and familiarity with biomedical metadata standards

  • Advanced Python and modern software-engineering practice; experience with database architecture, data tooling for biological workflows or AI coding assistants is highly valued

  • A pioneering mindset: self-driven, curious and motivated by turning advanced technology into real patient impact in an agile startup

Why join aiPTO

  • Direct patient impact: your work feeds models built for an aggressive cancer with few options — every well-structured dataset moves us closer to patient-matched therapy

  • Founding leadership: as our first Heidelberg team member you shape the technology stack, the architecture and the hub

  • World-class network: close collaboration with DKFZ, leading European clinical centres and international consortium partners

  • Package and trajectory: competitive compensation, hybrid working, and a career path that accelerates as aiPTO scales

title: Applied ML Engineer
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Applied ML Engineer based in Germany.

As an Applied ML Engineer, you’ll work at the intersection of machine learning research, experimentation, and production engineering.
You’ll turn ideas from research papers into rigorous experiments, measurable evidence, and reliable products.
The role spans model evaluation, model internals, inference infrastructure, backend systems, and user-facing product experiences.
You’ll work hands-on with modern ML models, designing evaluations that reveal what methods can—and cannot—demonstrate.
You’ll also build production-grade tooling that makes complex experiments repeatable, observable, and accessible to users.
The environment values technical judgment, ownership, scientific rigor, and the ability to move comfortably across the technology stack.
It’s an opportunity to help transform emerging ML techniques into practical systems that people can trust.


Accountabilities
  • Reproduce and evaluate machine learning research methods using open-weight and API-accessible models.
  • Design evaluation datasets, probes, scoring approaches, baselines, calibration tests, and experiment harnesses.
  • Work directly with model weights, logits, hidden states, activations, model APIs, and inference infrastructure when required.
  • Build and extend evaluation infrastructure covering experiment runners, judges, persistence, orchestration, reporting, and reproducibility.
  • Turn research workflows into intuitive product experiences, including experiment configuration, execution, traces, comparisons, reports, and review workflows.
  • Investigate how verification methods behave when models are modified through fine-tuning, merging, quantization, distillation, safety removal, or deliberate evasion.
  • Design controlled experiments that distinguish meaningful signals from artifacts, confounders, and misleading correlations.
  • Produce clear technical reports that separate measured evidence from interpretation and hypotheses.
  • Deliver production-quality systems with APIs, asynchronous jobs, databases, observability, testing, deployment, and documentation.
  • Contribute across research, experimentation, engineering, and product as priorities evolve.
  • During the first six months, reproduce and document at least one published model-provenance or verification method, including its capabilities, assumptions, and limitations.
  • Build a repeatable model-verification runner with versioned inputs, artifacts, metrics, and reports, and make at least one verification workflow accessible through the product interface.
  • Run controlled experiments across base, fine-tuned, merged, quantized, and known distilled models, improving understanding of when verification methods succeed, fail, and why.

    • Requirements:

    • Strong Python engineering skills, with hands-on experience using PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers.
    • Solid understanding of machine learning evaluation, including dataset design, baselines, metrics, calibration, false positives and negatives, statistical uncertainty, and reproducibility.
    • Ability to read ML research papers critically and implement methods from first principles rather than relying entirely on existing packages.
    • Professional software engineering experience beyond notebooks, including APIs, asynchronous jobs, databases, logging, testing, deployment, and documentation.
    • Familiarity with open-weight models and a practical understanding of how modern LLM inference systems operate.
    • Ability to work across backend and frontend boundaries, with sufficient React/TypeScript knowledge to help make complex experiments and results understandable to users.
    • Strong experimental and analytical judgment, particularly around distinguishing what evidence demonstrates from what it merely suggests.
    • High ownership and initiative, with the ability to identify problems, propose solutions, and drive projects forward independently.
    • Comfort working in a fast-moving startup environment where priorities can change quickly and engineers may operate across multiple functions.
    • Experience with model provenance, fingerprinting, watermarking, distillation detection, red-teaming, safety evaluation, interpretability, or related areas is a plus.
    • Experience with activation and representation analysis, probing, model hooks, logits, hidden states, or other model-internals techniques is advantageous.
    • Familiarity with evaluation and inference infrastructure such as DSPy, LiteLLM, Temporal, Ray, vLLM, PostgreSQL/pgvector, or comparable technologies is beneficial.
    • Experience with Next.js, React, TypeScript, data visualization, or experiment dashboards is a plus.

    • Experience designing adversarial evaluations or testing systems against deliberate attempts to evade detection is an advantage.
    • A strong commitment to producing production-quality code, tests, tooling, and documentation that other engineers can confidently operate and extend.

title: Senior Berater*in und Programm-Manager*in Kooperationen & Collective Impact (m/w/d)
description:
Dein neuer Job

Unsere Vision ist eine offene, nachhaltige und friedliche Gesellschaft, in der Gutes tun mit Wirkung das gemeinsame Handeln leitet. Um dazu unseren Beitrag zu leisten, haben wir PHINEO als gemeinnützige Plattform für strategisches gesellschaftliches Engagement aufgebaut.

Gesellschaftliche Herausforderungen lassen sich heute nur gemeinsam lösen. Deshalb arbeiten wir mit Unternehmen, Stiftungen, Sozialunternehmen, öffentlichen Institutionen und zivilgesellschaftlichen Organisationen daran, sektorübergreifende Zusammenarbeit zu stärken und mehr Wirkung zu erzielen. Für unser Team in Berlin suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt eine erfahrene Persönlichkeit, die Beratungs-, Netzwerk- und Gestaltungskompetenz miteinander verbindet, als Senior Berater*in und Programm-Manager*in Kooperationen & Collective Impact (m/w/d).


Deine Aufgaben

  • Du bringst Akteur*innen aus Wirtschaft, Zivilgesellschaft, Philanthropie und öffentlichem Sektor gezielt zusammen, um Kooperationen mit gesellschaftlichem Impact anzuregen. Dafür entwickelst du neue Formen der sektorübergreifenden Zusammenarbeit. Parallel gestaltest und moderierst du etablierte Dialogformate im analogen und digitalen Raum.
  • Du übernimmst eine zentrale Rolle bei IMPACT COLLECTIVES, unserem neuen Angebot, das Impact Startups mit Unternehmen, Investor*innen und weiteren Enablern aus Wissenschaft, Verwaltung und Zivilgesellschaft themenspezifisch verbinden wird und damit strukturellen Wandel entlang der großen gesellschaftlichen Herausforderungen unserer Zeit vorantreibt.
  • Du leitest unsere Corporate Citizenship Arbeitsgruppe, entwickelst sie strategisch weiter, gewinnst neue Unternehmen für die Mitwirkung. Du gestaltest gemeinsam mit Vertreter*innen aus Wirtschaft, Zivilgesellschaft und öffentlicher Hand Impulse für eine wirksame gesellschaftliche Verantwortung von Unternehmen.
  • Du konzipierst, akquirierst und verantwortest Beratungs- und Kooperationsprojekte. Beispielsweise berätst du Startups, die wissen möchten, wie sie mehr Impact erzielen oder Investor*innen finden können, oder begleitest Kooperationen zwischen Unternehmen und Nonprofits prozessual wie inhaltlich.
  • Du steuerst komplexe Projekte eigenverantwortlich von der Konzeption über das Partnermanagement bis zur Umsetzung und Auswertung. Handlungsleitend sind für dich der angestrebte gesellschaftliche Mehrwert und eine wirtschaftliche Umsetzung.
Bei der Arbeit bist du selbstverständlich nicht auf dich allein gestellt. Vielmehr bist du Teil eines engagierten Teams, das verschiedene Kompetenzen und Perspektiven vereint.


Das bringst Du mit

  • Du setzt dich mit Leidenschaft für gesellschaftliche Transformation, nachhaltiges Wirtschaften und die Zusammenarbeit von Akteur*innen aus unterschiedlichen gesellschaftlichen Bereichen ein.
  • Du bringst die Energie, Überzeugungskraft und Empathie mit, die es braucht, um Vertrauen aufzubauen und Menschen für gemeinsame Ziele zu gewinnen. Auch skeptische Akteur*innen kannst du inspirieren und aktivieren.
  • Du bringst Beratungserfahrung mit, idealerweise mit Startups, Investor*innen oder Unternehmen zu Fragen rund um Strategie oder Organisationentwicklung. Daher kannst du Beratungsprozesse konzipieren, eigenständig durchführen und zu belastbaren Ergebnissen führen.
  • Du hast in der Vergangenheit bereits Netzwerke aufgebaut oder intensiv betreut, idealerweise mit Beteiligung von Akteuren aus der Wirtschaft und aus dem Startup-Bereich. Du kannst relevante Akteure zeitnah identifizieren und sie mit unseren Zielgruppen vernetzen. Du besitzt Erfahrungen mit Multi-Stakeholder-Prozessen oder Collective-Impact-Ansätzen. Du bewegst dich sicher im Umgang mit Entscheider*innen auf Konzern- beziehungsweise Leitungsebene.
  • Du hast nachweisliche Erfahrung in der Entwicklung und Gewinnung von Partner*innen, Kund*innen oder Förder*innen sowie in der eigenverantwortlichen Leitung komplexer Projekte.


Deine Vorteile bei uns

Purpose

  • Ein sinnstiftender Job mit viel Gestaltungsspielraum.
  • Die Möglichkeit, an relevanten gesellschaftlichen Themen wie nachhaltige Wirtschaft, Stärkung von Demokratie und Klimaschutz mitzuarbeiten.
  • Eine Organisation, die danach strebt, eine Vielfalt an Identitäten, Erfahrungshintergründen und Perspektiven zusammenzubringen.
  • Ein großes Netzwerk an Kontakten aus Politik, Wirtschaft und Zivilgesellschaft.

Konditionen und Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten
  • 39 Stunden pro Woche in Vollzeit, Teilzeit bis zu 80% möglich.
  • Die Befristung des Arbeitsvertrages (2 Jahre) ist ein Punkt, an dem wir noch einmal gemeinsam reflektieren und eine bewusste Entscheidung treffen – hoffentlich füreinander. Sie ist ein Standard in all unseren neuen Arbeitsverhältnissen, um Achtsamkeit und Bewusstsein auf beiden Seiten der Beziehung zu stärken.
  • Diese Position liegt in unserer Stellengruppe 3 und ist beim aktuellen Aufgaben- und Verantwortungsspektrum bei einem Festgehalt zwischen 56.000 und 62.000 EUR verortet, abhängig von Erfahrung und Qualifikation. Arbeitszeitflexibilität und Familienfreundlichkeit
  • 30 Tage Urlaub im Jahr.

  • Die Möglichkeit, mobil zu arbeiten: sowohl regelmäßig im Inland als auch zwei Mal jährlich als Workation aus dem Ausland.
  • Eine Kultur, in der die Vereinbarkeit mit dem Privatleben einen hohen Stellenwert hat.

Klingt richtig gut? Dann bewirb dich mit deinen aussagekräftigen Unterlagen über unser Online-Bewerbungsformular. Wir sichten die Bewerbungen fortlaufend.

Coordination & reporting

Additionally, you'll enjoy 28 days of vacation every year, ensuring you have the time to recharge and explore your passions outside of work.
  • Vibrant Office in Central Berlin. Located in the digital heart of central Berlin, our bright office space fosters professional and personal interactions.

We help you find your place at ctrl QS, with a focus on your development goals. You’ll find fluid career paths with opportunities to specialize or grow laterally. Also, our internal Academy offers a wealth of learning opportunities.

Together, we form a multicultural and fun-loving team that thrives on collaboration.

About the Role

We're building WunderGraph Cosmo, the open-source GraphQL Federation solution. Probably the most important component of Cosmo is the Cosmo Router, which - simply put - connects all API endpoints and handles the GraphQL requests and responses whilst applying the Federation protocol (among other magical things, like normalization, execution planning etc.). Fully written in Go, it's the fastest GraphQL Router available and a quite potent (and complex) piece of cutting-edge open-source software. How about joining our team to make it even better and strap the rocket boosters onto GraphQL Federation?

 

TEAM INTEGRATION

You will be in charge of

  • Develop, refactor and maintain GraphQL Go Tools' (Router) open-source code base in Golang (low GC code)

  • Run internal penetration tests of the Router

  • Troubleshoot Router issues, potentially together with our customers' engineers

  • Analyze and accept up open-source contributions on Github

     

The "Engine" is essentially a Golang application which translates GraphQL requests into any other protocol, like OpenAPI, SOAP, gRPC, GraphQL, Apollo Federation, etc. You could consider the Engine as a "GraphQL Compiler" or Transpiler. The Engine is responsible for parsing, normalization, execution planning, execution runtime, etc... If you are interested in working with ASTs, AST transformations, etc... you will love this kind of work. We have performance requirements, so you should be proficient in writing performant and low GC code in Golang.

Some of your tasks will take more than a few weeks to complete, Ideally, you're someone who likes to go deep on one topic instead of going wide and shallow on many different topics.

Why WunderGraph?

  • Pick your preferred work hardware

  • We focus on getting stuff done, and on having fun whilst doing so: work hard, play hard!

title: Staff Data Engineer
description:
We're seeking a Staff Data Engineer to join one of the fastest-growing AI legal tech companies in Europe. You'll take technical ownership of the data platform behind how we run the business: the pipelines, the warehouse, and the definitions behind the numbers our leadership team actually uses.

You'll report to our Head of Engineering and work alongside a colleague who owns the business-facing side of data, plus our infrastructure and application engineers. This is a senior individual contributor role with no line management in either direction, roughly 70% hands-on building, 30% defining, documenting and explaining.

Your Challenge and Opportunity in This Role

JUPUS supports hundreds of law firms across Europe, and our customer base is growing roughly 4x a year. Our data platform has grown with it (ClickHouse, dbt, Python extract-load pipelines into an S3 data lake, orchestration in GitHub Actions) and it has grown fast.

Your job is to make it trustworthy. That means modernising what already exists, making historical trends a record of what actually happened rather than a nightly re-derivation of it, and owning the definitions behind the metrics that reach our board. This is not a greenfield build, and it is not a maintenance seat. It is a real platform with real problems, and you would own it.

Tasks

  • Own the data platform end to end: ingestion and the raw layer, the ClickHouse warehouse, and the dbt project on top of it. You're the person who can say whether a number is wrong or the pipeline is.

  • Make our numbers trustworthy: reliability, correctness, and a history that holds up, so that a trend is a record of what actually happened rather than a re-derivation of it.

  • Own the metrics the company runs on, starting with our customer health score- the definition, the denominator, the eligibility rules and the known limitations, not just the SQL underneath them.

  • Turn business questions into durable metrics: work directly with Customer Success, Sales, Product and leadership to understand what they're actually trying to decide, then build something defensible enough to decide on.

  • Keep cost and complexity in check as we grow: warehouse architecture, query cost, and the surfaces that deliver data into BI and our CRM. All of it gets harder as the customer base multiplies.

  • Set the standard for how data work is done here: one authoritative written definition per leadership-visible number, and the conventions that inform our Data function as it grows with us.

Requirements

Technical Expertise

  • Substantial experience in data engineering or analytics engineering, with production ownership of a warehouse and a transformation layer. We care more about evidence of ownership than about years served.

  • ClickHouse in production.

  • dbt at ownership level: incremental models, snapshots, tests, macros, CI/CD. Ideally you've inherited someone else's dbt project and left it better than you found it.

  • Python data engineering: EL tooling, S3, CI-based orchestration that you’ve owned end to end, with no platform team behind you.

  • Product event streams: PostHog, Amplitude, Segment, Mixpanel or similar. You understand how user-to-company identity and group association break, and what that does to every metric downstream.

Judgement and Ownership

  • You have defined a business KPI end to end and defended it to non-technical people. This is the differentiator for us. An excellent engineer who takes requirements as given is not the right fit for this role.

  • Analytical rigour: cohorts, correct denominators, sample size stated before findings. You'll say "we can't tell yet, and here's exactly why" rather than produce a confident chart.

  • You act without waiting for a ticket, and you can name something you chose to stop doing.

  • You're comfortable in front of senior stakeholders, including C-level, and can hold a technical line without losing the room.

Further Requirements

  • Located within CET +/-2.

  • Nice to have: BI tool administration (we use Metabase), CRM and billing systems as data sources, dlt specifically, GDPR-driven data deletion work, Grafana, German, or B2B SaaS and legal-tech domain experience.

  • Nice to have: you're used to non-technical colleagues querying data through AI tools, and you design for that.

Benefits

🎯 Metric Ownership – Own a business-critical metric end to end, definition included — not just the pipeline that feeds it.

🛠️ A Real Platform – ClickHouse and dbt already in production, with genuine problems worth solving. No greenfield theatre, no maintenance seat.

⚡ Direct Access – A flat structure and a direct line to our Head of Engineering, CTO and CEO. No committee between you and a decision.

📈 Growth Stage – Roughly 4x customer growth a year at one of Europe's fastest-growing AI legal tech companies.

🏡 Fully Remote – Enjoy the flexibility of working from anywhere

💻 Top Equipment – State-of-the-art MacBook plus all the accessories you need

🏋️ Wellbeing Perks – Urban Sports Club membership to support your healthy lifestyle

Unsere Überzeugungen: Wir stellen nach Fähigkeiten und Potenzial ein. Mit über 80 Nationalitäten, 45 % Frauen im Unternehmen und 56 % Frauen in unserem Leadership-Team ist Diversität kein Programm – sie ist Teil unserer DNA. Wir suchen Menschen, die experimentieren, ohne auf Erlaubnis zu warten, KI über das Offensichtliche hinaus nutzen und wissen, wann man ihr vertrauen kann - und wann man sie hinterfragen sollte. 

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Join us as an Anti-Financial Crime Working Student or Intern to improve the operational processes behind Qonto’s German branch. You’ll join our Central Europe AFC team and begin with a high-impact challenge: making sure sensitive physical correspondence—including court documents, legal notices, seizures, and law-enforcement requests—is received, routed, tracked, and handled on time. As you gain autonomy, you’ll connect teams across AFC, Banking Operations, Legal, and Product while helping us build clearer and more reliable ways of working.

➡️ As an Anti-Financial Crime Working Student or Intern at Qonto, you will:
  • Improve a critical operational process: Map our current physical-mail workflow, understand how documents move from our external provider to internal teams, and identify unclear ownership, bottlenecks, and missed handoffs.
  • Build a reliable coordination system: Help design and maintain clear routing rules, trackers, ownership models, escalation paths, and follow-up routines so sensitive requests reach the right people on time.
  • Connect teams across Qonto: Coordinate with AFC, AML, Fraud, Banking Operations, Legal, and other stakeholders to gather information, clarify responsibilities, and maintain visibility on open actions.
  • Support AFC and Product projects: Once the core workflow is stable, help organize our Product × AFC feature-approval process, including coordinating input from multiple MLROs across Europe.
  • Improve how we work with AI: Experiment with AI to structure information, document workflows, prepare updates, and reduce repetitive coordination work—while checking outputs carefully and protecting sensitive information.


 ➡️ What you can expect:
  • A concrete project with visible impact: Your first mission addresses an important operational risk for Qonto’s German branch. Your work will contribute directly to the timely handling of sensitive banking and legal procedures.
  • Broad exposure across Qonto: You’ll work beyond a single team and gain insight into AFC, operations, legal, product, growth, and marketing within Germany—Qonto’s second-largest branch.
  • Real ownership: This is project-based work rather than a list of repetitive daily tasks. You’ll be expected to investigate problems, propose practical solutions, and turn them into sustainable processes.
  • Progressive scope: You’ll begin with the physical-mail workflow. As you establish a reliable process, you’ll take on additional coordination projects across AFC and Product.
  • Hybrid work in Berlin: Approximately 3 days per week in the office to support learning and collaboration.


 ➡️ About You:
  • You are an enrolled student: You may be pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Law, Economics, Marketing, or another relevant field. We are open to different academic backgrounds and do not require a specific specialization.
  • You are autonomous and accountable: You can take a loosely defined problem, ask the right questions, structure your approach, and make concrete progress without waiting for step-by-step instructions.
  • You are organized and rigorous: You can track several stakeholders, owners, deadlines, and dependencies while understanding why small gaps matter when legal or regulatory requests are involved.
  • You learn quickly: Previous AFC or banking experience is not required, but you are curious about financial crime, banking operations, legal processes, and how a fintech works.
  • You are comfortable with digital tools: You can work confidently with Google Workspace. Familiarity with Notion is particularly useful.
  • You have professional English: English is the team’s working language. German is a plus, but it is not mandatory; Dutch is an additional bonus.
  • You are curious about AI: You are willing to experiment with AI to organize information and improve processes while maintaining accuracy, judgment, and confidentiality.


About your future Manager:
You manager will be Stefano, Anti-Financial Crime Director for Central Europe and Oversight and Deputy Managing Director for Germany. He’ll give you the context and support needed to understand sensitive AFC and banking processes while trusting you to investigate problems, propose solutions, and progressively take ownership.

  • His background? Stefano joined Qonto in 2025 after nearly a decade in AML and compliance roles across banking and crypto, including Senior Manager for Risk & Compliance at PwC, AML and Compliance Officer at Coinbase Germany and Upvest, and earlier compliance positions at Intesa Sanpaolo and Deutsche Bank. At Qonto, he oversees Anti-Financial Crime topics across Central Europe and contributes to the governance of the German branch.
  • What he brings to the team? A combination of regulatory perspective, cross-market experience, and an autonomous management style. Stefano does not micromanage: he creates space to test ideas and solve problems independently while remaining available for daily guidance, brainstorming, and regular project checkpoints.

Bleib aktiv. Mit Gympass hast du Zugang zu über 50 Sport- und Wellnesspartnern.

Sei du selbst. Ein inklusives, unterstützendes Umfeld, in dem alle willkommen sind.

title: Technical Product Manager
description:
This role starts on the content platform, and the platform surface it serves is growing. The foundations of the company, identity and access, developer platform, data and the infrastructure everything runs on, are being invested in over the coming year. We are looking for someone whose curiosity does not stop at the edge of their own team, because the interesting problems here sit exactly where those layers meet. 

There is genuine ambiguity in this space right now, and a decision or two you would inherit that we have not finished making. We would rather tell you that than have you discover it in month two. The upside is that very little here is set, so the person who takes this shapes the layer everything else in the product is built on for the next several years. 

Requirements

  • Own the content services every surface depends on. The services and APIs that serve content to the learner surface, the admin surface and everything we build next, plus the delivery path including CDN and video, and file and asset storage. 
  • Own the structural contract. How content is stored, versioned and served so it can be reused and assembled differently for different customers. This is a schema and interface problem before it is a tooling problem, and your measure is whether the contract other teams build against is clear, stable and safe to change. 
  • Own multi tenant separation. Making sure one customer’s content and branding stay theirs. The tenancy model needs a decision and an owner, and that will be one of your first real pieces of work. 
  • Own access, entitlements and data residency. Who can reach what, where data lives, and what we are able to commit to contractually. 
  • Own performance and cost per tenant. If this layer is slow, everything is slow. If it is expensive, it is expensive everywhere. 
  • Carry the platform half of a migration already in flight. We are moving off an incumbent content tool while the current system keeps earning. Sequencing that is the real work, and the order matters more than the ambition. 
  • Own the non functional questions that show up in deals. A meaningful share of our deals slow down in security and compliance review rather than in the pitch, and that is a product problem with a revenue number attached. 

This role is for you if you have:

  • Experience with content management as a product, whether that is a CMS, a DAM, a headless content platform or a structured content system at scale. This is our primary preference. 
  • Experience owning platform or infrastructure adjacent product, where success was measured in what other teams could build rather than in features a customer names. 
  • Enough technical depth to be useful and the honesty to say where you are not. You can read an architecture proposal, ask the question that unpicks it, and tell the difference between a researched answer and a fluent one. 
  • The ability to hold your own with senior engineers, infrastructure engineers and security specialists. Not as a peer on implementation, but well enough that a remediation estimate or a tenancy design does not go unchallenged. A previous career as an engineer is a real advantage and not a requirement. 
  • A habit of thinking in seams. Where systems meet, what a contract between them should guarantee, and how to keep a decision reversible rather than walking through a one way door. 
  • The ability to sequence. We are modernising a platform that carries real history while it keeps earning, and the order matters more than the ambition. 
  • Writing. Decisions, tradeoffs and the reasoning behind them, in a way an engineer and an executive can both act on. 
  • Nice to have, and genuinely useful: depth in AI and personalisation, or in infrastructure. Either one compounds with this role, and we are not expecting both. 

This role is not for you if:

  • You want to be a delivery manager for the engineers. They are strong and they do not need coordinating. They need decisions and clarity about what matters. 
  • You want to own the authoring and editorial experience itself. A colleague owns that, you will work closely with them, and drawing the seam between you well is part of the job. 
  • You want to run a rewrite programme. Foundations serve outcomes, and a foundation with no customer outcome attached does not get funded here and should not. 
  • You need the surrounding decisions settled before you arrive.

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
We are growing this team while it delivers, on a platform with real history, and some of what we currently believe will turn out to be wrong. The incumbent HR suites are consolidating and buying their way into this space, so the clock is real. 

The problem underneath it is genuinely unsolved. Nobody has built software that knows what a person needs to be able to do next week, teaches it in the few minutes they actually have, and observes whether it landed without asking them. Not the language apps, which have the habit but not the stakes. Not the platforms, which have the content but not the attention. Not the HR suites, which have the data but have never made anything a person voluntarily opens. 

If that sounds like a problem worth several years, we should talk. 

As our Senior Product Manager for the learner experience, you own the surface where learning actually happens, for the person actually doing it. It is the most visible product role in the company, because everything else in our strategy depends on somebody coming back on a Tuesday. Today weekly active learners sits close to one percent. That number is the job. 

Requirements

  • Own the learner surface end to end. Onboarding, what someone is offered next, how it arrives, and what we learn from what they did. 
  • Move us from a catalogue people browse to a product that pays attention. Personalisation here is a spectrum, not a feature: country and industry, company size, whether they reach us through their own LMS or directly, then company, department, team and finally the individual. A fifteen minute bus ride should be able to become seven minutes of audio and three quick questions, assembled for that person. 
  • Partner with our educational designers on how it reaches one person. They have decades of research behind how our content is built, in activities of two to eight minutes designed for habit formation. What is not yet settled is how those pieces compose into a path for one person, and you would be one of the people settling it. Your half is the one they cannot do on their own: how it reaches one specific person, on one specific day, on whatever device they have, and what to offer instead when something did not land. 
  • Own the measurement that makes it real. Weekly active learners is the number this role moves. There is a baseline. Setting the target with us, and owning the path to it, is part of the job. 
  • Treat mobile as a first class question rather than a port. Seven minutes attached to a real week is a phone experience far more often than a desk one. Whether that is a native client or something lighter is a genuine open decision with very different costs. 
  • Draw on a single library. Our own studio content, customer created content and content generated on the spot all sit together, and deciding what surfaces to whom is part of your job. 

This role is for you if you have 

  • A track record owning either a B2B2C product, where the buyer and the user are different people and the user did not choose you, or a consumer habit-formation product built to create usage rather than meet demand that already existed 
  • Evidence you have shipped personalisation, routing or recommendation work that measurably changed behaviour, and the scar tissue to know how often it does not 
  • Comfort on a platform that carries real history. You will build the new thing while the old thing earns the revenue, and sequencing that is part of the craft rather than an obstacle to it 
  • A habit of deciding. You gather input properly and then take the call, and you can say clearly what you are not doing and why 
  • A habit of working in the open. Drafts early, thinking visible, and you would rather be corrected on Tuesday than right on Friday 
  • A genuine interest in how people learn. You do not need a background in it, you do need to find it interesting, because you will work closely with people who have spent careers on it 
  • Comfort partnering with an embedded engineering manager on the team rather than managing engineers directly 

This role is not for you if 

  • You want a clean greenfield. That is a much easier engineering problem and a much worse bet, and it is not what this is 
  • You need the strategy finished before you start. It is being written now and you would be one of the people writing it 
  • You want to run the roadmap process. Product Operations owns that craft, this role owns the outcome

title: Senior Backend Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
Unsere Opportunity

Predium hat in den letzten drei Jahren die führende ESG-Intelligence-Plattform für institutionelle Immobilienunternehmen in der DACH-Region gebaut - mit den stärksten Namen der Branche als Kunden: Asset Manager, Wohnungsbaugesellschaften, Banken. Unsere Kundenbasis, die Daten, unsere Glaubwürdigkeit sind wertvolles Kapital für den nächsten Schritt. Investment-, Kredit- und Asset-Management-Entscheidung werden in der Real Estate Branche noch immer in Excel getroffen, Fall für Fall. Wir bauen jetzt den AI-Analysten, der diese Arbeit übernimmt. Direkt auf den Daten des Kunden, skalierbar ohne zusätzliche Köpfe. Wir sind stark finanziert und bringen KI in die Real Estate Branche.

Deine Mission

Als Senior Backend Engineer verantwortest du die Systeme hinter unserer Plattform: die GraphQL-API, das relationale Datenmodell, die Hintergrundverarbeitung, die Dokumente und Excel-Dateien unserer Kunden in strukturierte Daten verwandelt, und das Berechtigungsmodell, mit dem ein einzelner Eigentümer und eine Bank mit hunderten Portfolios dasselbe Produkt nutzen. Der Großteil deiner Arbeit läuft vom Schema-Design bis zum Resolver.
Du arbeitest eng mit Product, Design und den anderen Engineers zusammen, damit wir das bauen, was zählt - nicht nur das, was dir gesagt wurde. Du übernimmst echte Verantwortung für Production: Wenn etwas langsam ist, findest du heraus, warum – egal ob die Antwort eine schlechte Query, Anwendungscode oder die Infrastruktur darunter ist.
Du hilfst uns außerdem, KI in Production zuverlässig zu machen. Dokumentenextraktion, lang laufende Analyse-Jobs und agentische Features sind zentral für die Richtung des Produkts - und wir brauchen Leute, die diese Workflows testbar und verlässlich machen, statt nur in der Demo beeindruckend.
Bei uns gewinnt die beste Idee - egal von wem sie kommt. Mit 40 Leuten gibt's einfach keinen Raum für Politik. Und: Jede Zeile Code trägt dazu bei, den CO2-Fußabdruck von Immobilien zu verbessern.

Tech-Stack: TypeScript (NestJS im Backend, React im Frontend), Hasura/GraphQL, PostgreSQL (mehrere Datenbanken inkl. PostGIS), Queue-basierte Job-Verarbeitung, AWS (ECS / Elastic Beanstalk, S3, SES, Textract), Infrastructure-as-Code, Claude

Was du konkret tust

  • Du baust Features über unsere Hasura GraphQL-API, NestJS und Postgres - vom Schema-Design bis zum Resolver.
  • Du modellierst komplexe Immobilien- und ESG-Domänen in relationalen Schemas. Wir betreiben mehrere Postgres-Datenbanken parallel (eine davon geospatial), und Schema-Entscheidungen haben hier langfristige Konsequenzen.
  • Du verantwortest die Hintergrundverarbeitung: Excel-Importe, Dokumentenextraktion, lang laufende Analyse-Jobs. Queues, Retries, Jobs, die andere Jobs starten - und die Frage, was passiert, wenn Schritt 3 von 7 um 2 Uhr nachts fehlschlägt.
  • Du entwickelst unser Berechtigungsmodell weiter. Unsere Kunden reichen vom einzelnen Eigentümer bis zum Konzern mit Zugriff auf Organisations-, Portfolio- und Gebäudeebene. Das richtig zu bauen ist echte Design-Arbeit, keine Middleware-Konfiguration.
  • Du integrierst LLMs in Backend-Workflows - vor allem für Dokumenten- und Datenextraktion - und machst sie zuverlässig und testbar.
  • Du debuggst Production. Du nutzt Grafana Dashboards und Traces, um herauszufinden, warum etwas langsam ist oder fehlschlägt - ob in der App, der CI/Build-Pipeline oder der Infrastruktur.
  • Du erkennst überwucherte oder unnötig komplexe Teile der Codebase und vereinfachst sie, ohne dass dich jemand darum bitten muss. Komplexität abzubauen gehört zum Job, ist kein Nebenprojekt.

Woran wir Erfolg messen

  • Du hast Features end-to-end über Schema, API und Hintergrundverarbeitung ausgeliefert, die unsere Kunden aktiv nutzen.
  • Unsere asynchrone Verarbeitung (Importe, Extraktion, Analyse-Jobs) ist messbar robuster: weniger stille Fehler, klare Retry- und Recovery-Pfade und Observability, die uns sagt, was kaputt ist und warum.
  • Du hast Ownership für mindestens einen Kernbereich übernommen - z. B. das Berechtigungsmodell, die Job-Orchestrierung oder die LLM-Extraktions-Pipeline - und bist dafür die Anlaufstelle im Team.
  • Du hast Testing und Developer Experience im Backend auf ein neues Level gehoben, und andere Engineers liefern dadurch schneller.
  • Du bist für Product und das Team ein verlässlicher Sparringspartner, wenn wir entscheiden, was wir bauen und wie.

Was du mitbringst

  • Du bist stark in Postgres. Schema-Design fällt dir leicht, du kannst einen Query Plan lesen und weißt, wann das ORM dich anlügt. Geospatial-Erfahrung ist ein Bonus, keine Voraussetzung.
  • Du bist fließend in typisiertem Backend-TypeScript. Wir arbeiten täglich mit NestJS und GraphQL; wenn deine Erfahrung aus einem vergleichbaren Stack kommt, ist das völlig okay - du arbeitest dich ein.
  • Du hast echte Queue-basierte Verarbeitung gebaut. Nicht „ich habe mal einen Job in eine Queue gelegt", sondern Worker designt, Retries und Teilausfälle behandelt, mehrstufige Workflows orchestriert.
  • Du hast Authorization für ein Multi-Tenant-Produkt designt und weißt, wo es haarig wird.
  • Du hast lieber einen Integrationstest gegen eine echte Datenbank als zehn Unit-Tests, die alles mocken. Du schreibst den Test, der die kaputte Migration erwischt.
  • Du behandelst Production als debuggbares System. Du findest über Dashboards und Traces heraus, warum etwas langsam ist, und Infrastruktur ist für dich nicht das Problem von jemand anderem.
  • Du kommunizierst klar - mit Engineers, Product und bei Bedarf direkt mit Kunden.
  • Du sprichst Deutsch auf C1-Niveau oder besser und fließend Englisch. Unsere Kunden sind deutsche Banken und Asset Manager, und du wirst mit ihnen sprechen.

Bonus:

  • AWS (S3, SES, ECS, RDS, …) sowie Infrastructure-as-Code.
  • LLMs in Production, vor allem Dokumenten- oder Datenextraktion - und die Fähigkeit, sie zuverlässig statt nur beeindruckend zu machen.
  • Data-Pipeline-Erfahrung: stufenweise, reproduzierbare Verarbeitung, Dataset-Versionierung.
  • Mentoring oder Führung von Engineers - oder der Wunsch, da reinzuwachsen.
  • Debugging von Tooling- und Build-Problemen, nicht nur von Anwendungscode. Unsere Toolchain entwickelt sich schnell und ist gelegentlich nicht Standard.

Warum Predium?

  • Stage: ~40 Leute, stark finanziert, auf dem Weg die Kategorie zu definieren. Früh genug, dass vieles noch gebaut werden muss. Ja, es ist manchmal messy - aber genau das ist der Punkt. Wenn du einen fertigen Playbook-Job suchst, ist das hier nicht der richtige Fit.
  • Impact: Du bist nicht Rädchen #100 in einer Company. Was du hier baust, ist das, worauf sich unsere Kunden jeden Tag verlassen. Dein Beitrag ist direkt sichtbar, im Revenue und im Produkt.
  • Ownership: Wir managen nicht deine Zeit, wir messen deine Ergebnisse. Du bekommst Verantwortung und Freiraum - und die Erwartung, beides zu nutzen.
  • Compensation: Competitive Salary, Bonus und Equity-Beteiligung. Wir wollen, dass du am Erfolg partizipierst, den du mitaufbaust.
  • Team: Office-first im Werksviertel München, 4 Tage/Woche.

title: GTM Growth Manager
description:
Voice is becoming the primary interface for technology. For the first time in history, we can use natural language to control and interact with our devices, services, and applications, and we’re only at the beginning of the adoption of Voice and Physical AI across industries. Current voice interactions, however, still lack a fundamental human skill: nuanced understanding of audio scenes and environments. Navigating complex auditory scenes, distinguishing between multiple voices, or focusing on a main speaker are all part of the challenge of “teaching machines to hear like human beings.”

At ai-coustics, we’re building the audio intelligence layer and developer tooling to enable more robust and intelligent voice agents and Physical AI applications. Today, Voice AI companies like Perplexity, Retell, LiveKit or AssemblyAI use the ai-coustics SDK to prepare their agents for real-world acoustic challenges. Our models power thousands of agents worldwide and process millions of hours each month.

We are backed by leading early-stage investors including Connect Ventures, Partech, Inovia Capital, as well as angel investors from HuggingFace, DeepMind and Amazon with deep expertise in AI and developer infrastructure. These partners share our vision and are helping us build a world-class team operating with high levels of responsibility and velocity. We look for people who take ownership, think systemically, and want to solve challenging real-world problems in close collaboration with our customers. If you’re motivated by developing technology that is used in practice, shaping an emerging category and setting a new standard for how Voice AI works in the real world, you’ll feel at home at ai-coustics.

About the role

Developers find us, install the SDK, and start processing audio before we ever speak to them. Thousands of accounts have run audio through our models. Some become customers, but many sit somewhere between a first test and real production use. The opportunity is to identify the accounts with real potential, understand what moves them from testing to paying, and find what makes them grow from there.

You own that journey, from reaching promising developers and teams to converting and growing them. You use product and usage data to decide where to focus, get involved in promising evaluations early, and close startup and mid-market deals. You also experiment with outbound approaches to reach new prospects, identify ways to expand existing customers, and build and test the pricing and operational systems that make the whole motion work.

This isn't a conventional sales role or a RevOps role. It is a job for someone who wants to do both. If you only want to close, this will frustrate you. If you only want to analyse, you'll be uncomfortable when a number depends on you picking up the phone.

Tasks

  • Signup to paid — Carry the conversion number. Work out which trials are real, get into the evaluation early, cut time-to-value, and remove what's blocking the purchase.
  • Outbound — Own the motion end to end: target lists, sequencing, messaging, cadence, and the tooling. Run experiments and double down on what converts.
  • Full-cycle sales — Run startup and mid-market deals end to end: discovery, qualification, technical evaluation, pricing, negotiation, close.
  • Expansion and retention — Own NRR. Most start on one model and a fraction of their traffic. Find the next use case, catch the accounts going quiet before they churn, win back the ones that left.
  • Account intelligence — Build the scoring layer. Turn usage data into a ranked list, and keep the ICP current as the market moves.
  • Rev ops and reporting — Own HubSpot, the funnel model and the monthly numbers. You keep them accurate because we make decisions from them, and everyone from the board down reads the numbers you produce.
  • Pricing and packaging — Run experiments on the self-serve tiers: what's in each plan, where the limits sit, what triggers an upgrade. Ship, measure, roll out what lifts conversion.
  • AI-native operations — Build agents and automations across your whole role, pipeline generation to revenue operations. We already run this way and you'll extend it.
  • Voice of customer — Gather feedback from customer interactions so product knows what to build and marketing knows how to position.

Requirements

  • 2–5 years in a commercial role at a startup or scale-up, ideally with an AI, developer, API or infrastructure product, where you carried a number and personally owned part of a funnel. You've worked somewhere growing fast and know what it's like when the playbook doesn't exist yet, the targets move, and nobody hands you a territory.
  • You've closed. You can talk about specific deals you won and lost, and what you'd do differently.
  • Love data. You can build a funnel in a product analytics tool, interrogate a CRM, write a query to check a hunch, and spot when a number is lying to you. We use PostHog and HubSpot.
  • Experiment discipline. You can design a test, judge whether the result means anything, and say so when it doesn't.
  • Tool fluency. Claude Code, Codex, Lemlist, HubSpot, PostHog. You're fast on the stack and faster picking up what's next.
  • Comfortable with a technical buyer. You can follow a conversation about latency, benchmarks, SDK integration and model behaviour, ask useful questions, and know when to bring an engineer in.
  • You sell the way developers buy. Our customers evaluate before they talk to anyone and respond to evidence.
  • You use AI daily as an operational tool, not an experiment. You build workflows with it and have opinions about where it helps and where it produces noise.
  • Strong copywriting skills and written communication. You're able to A/B test copy and see what customers respond to.
  • High agency. You're joining a commercial team still being built, with no established playbook. Your instinct should be to go and find out rather than wait to be briefed.
  • Commercial generalist. You're comfortable wearing several hats in a day and don't wait for someone to define the lane.
  • Working language is English. German is useful and not required.
  • Bonus: you've worked in voice AI, speech or audio before. Not a requirement, but it will shorten your first month. Our customers are building voice agents and the vocabulary is specific. Caring about sound and how it works helps.

Benefits

  • Opportunity to work at a rapidly growing Voice AI startup, backed by top investors.
  • Compensation and equity: Competitive salary package, additional benefits and stock options, enabling you to take part in the company’s success.
  • Startup Culture: Dynamic, fast-paced environment with passionate and collaborative colleagues.
  • High Impact: Groundbreaking startup at a pivotal growth stage, making a real difference in how people experience audio.
  • Ownership & Autonomy: Take full ownership of projects and ship fast.
  • Work With the Best: World-class team of engineers and builders with ample room for professional growth.
  • Contribute to the Future: Define the landscape of Voice AI technology.

If you are ready to lead the charge in revolutionizing Voice AI and drive our startup to new heights, we would love to hear from you. Apply today to join the ai-coustics team!
